Alaska with Mom — Made Simple

Kim, this proposal is built just for the two of you — you and your mom. Every excursion is selected with comfort, pace, and accessibility in mind, while still delivering the full Alaska magic. Next: Seattle Hotel
Pre-Cruise Stay · Seattle

Mayflower Park Hotel

Historic · Downtown · Steps from Pike Place · Welcoming Guests Since 1927
Mayflower Park Hotel
405 Olive Way, Downtown Seattle · 3 miles from Pier 91
Live Rate · 1 Night · 2 Guests · June 8
Live Pricing from Kayak / Booking.com
from$200
~$200–$268/night in June · Taxes additional
The Mayflower Park is the perfect landing spot for you and Mom. It's one of Seattle's last independently owned historic hotels — approaching its 100th anniversary in 2027. The Queen Suite (2 closets, 2 bathrooms, sitting room) has been specifically praised by guests traveling with elderly companions. Check-in wine vouchers at Oliver's Lounge are included for both guests. Pike Place Market is a 10-minute stroll. The concierge can arrange your Pier 91 transfer for the next morning.

Downtown Seattle — walkable to everything

Agent's Note: Previous guests with elderly companions specifically called out the Queen Suite for its two bathrooms and sitting room — it removes any "sharing a space" awkwardness and gives Mom her own area to rest. Request a higher floor for quieter rooms. Book directly with the hotel or through me for best rate flexibility and cancellation terms. Discovery Princess

Day by Day

Your 7-Night Alaska Journey

Here's exactly what each day looks like. I've noted which days are best for resting on the balcony versus going ashore. Everything is paced with Mom's comfort in mind — there are no days that require rushing or long walks.
Day 1 · June 9
Embarkation — Seattle, Washington
AM
Leisurely breakfast at Andaluca, then checkout from Mayflower Park · Rideshare or taxi to Pier 91 (~$20)
11 AM
Pier 91 opens for boarding · Mini-suite guests board with priority access · Champagne welcome in your cabin
4:00 PM
Sail away from Seattle · Enjoy the Seattle skyline from your balcony with a glass of bubbly
Day 2 · June 10
Sea Day — Inside Passage Scenic Sailing
All Day
Balcony day. Glide through the legendary Inside Passage. Watch for bald eagles, humpback whales, and sea otters. Reserve your spa treatment, explore the ship, or settle into the Reserve Dining Room for a leisurely lunch.
Evening
Broadway-style show in the Princess Theatre · Casino opens · Movies Under the Stars on the pool deck
Day 3 · June 11
Ketchikan — Salmon Capital of the World
7:00 AM
Dock downtown Ketchikan · Walk off the gangway onto Creek Street — no tender needed
All Day
Creek Street historic boardwalk (flat, easy walking) · Totem Heritage Center (air-conditioned museum) · Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show (covered, seated audience)
4:00 PM
Back aboard · Depart Ketchikan northbound
Day 4 · June 12
Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier — Scenic Sailing
Morning
The day you'll talk about forever. No going ashore — the ship sails deep into Endicott Arm Fjord. Watch Dawes Glacier calve massive walls of ice into the sea. Towering granite cliffs on both sides. Rangers narrate over the ship's speakers.
All Day
Stay on your private balcony or at the bow deck · Binoculars recommended · Have warm drinks delivered via the Princess app · No rushing, no schedules
Day 5 · June 13
Juneau — Alaska's Capital · More Ashore Late Night
7:00 AM
Arrive Juneau — accessible only by sea or air, making it feel delightfully remote
All Day
Mount Roberts Tramway (seated gondola — ideal for Mom) · Browse Juneau's historic downtown · Local salmon bake dinner ashore · Optional whale watching catamaran
9:00 PM
More Ashore: ship stays until 9 PM — rare extended evening · Enjoy dinner ashore without rushing back
Day 6 · June 14
Skagway — 🚂 White Pass & Yukon Route Railway
7:00 AM
Arrive Skagway · Dock steps from the historic gold rush downtown — no shuttle needed
9:00 AM
🚂 White Pass & Yukon Route Railway departs. Board the historic narrow-gauge train for a 3-hour roundtrip journey to the Canadian border. Comfortable heated cars, panoramic windows, breathtaking mountain and trestle scenery. This is exactly what you asked for — and it's perfect for Mom.
Afternoon
Return to Skagway · Browse gold rush-era shops on Broadway Street · Klondike Gold Rush National Park is a short stroll (flat, paved, ranger-led)
4:30 PM
Back aboard · Sail south toward Victoria
Day 7 · June 15
Victoria, British Columbia
5:30 PM
Evening port call in Canada's most charming city · Inner Harbour is steps from the dock · Butchart Gardens illuminated at night (shuttle available) · Afternoon tea at The Fairmont Empress Hotel
11:00 PM
Depart Victoria · Overnight sail south to Seattle
Day 8 · June 16
Disembarkation — Seattle · Fly Home to Shreveport
7:00 AM
Arrive Seattle Pier 91 · Disembark · Rideshare to Seattle-Tacoma International (SEA) · Fly home to Shreveport
Next: Shore Excursions for You & Mom
Experiences Ashore

Excursions — Selected for You & Mom

I've curated this list specifically for two travelers where comfort and accessibility matter. Every option here is either seated, covered, or low-impact. Prices shown are per person unless noted. The White Pass Railway is highlighted — book it as soon as your cruise is confirmed, as it sells out months ahead. Senior rates are noted where available.
PORT: KETCHIKAN
Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show
Covered outdoor arena · Seated bleachers · 60-minute show · Chopping, sawing, log rolling, axe throwing · Entertaining for all ages · No mobility concerns · Easy walk from ship
$40–$55/pp Senior pricing available
Creek Street Historic Walk & Totem Heritage Center
Self-guided or narrated · Flat boardwalk (wheelchair accessible) · World's largest collection of standing totems · Covered museum portion · Perfect low-key morning while ship is in port
$20–$40/pp · Museum entry ~$15
Ketchikan Harbor Sightseeing Boat Tour
Seated tour boat · No walking · Harbor and channel views · Local guide narrates salmon and Alaska history · 90 minutes · Climate-controlled cabin available · Ideal for Mom
$55–$80/pp Senior-friendly
PORT: JUNEAU
Mount Roberts Tramway
Scenic gondola ride to 1,800 ft · Fully seated · No hiking required · Panoramic views of Juneau and the Inside Passage from the observation deck · Nature center and restaurant at the top · Accessible for all mobility levels · One of the best views in Alaska
$35–$45/pp Senior rate ~$32
Mendenhall Glacier Bus Tour (Narrated)
Comfortable motorcoach to the glacier visitor center · Short flat walk to the viewing platform · See a living glacier up close · Ranger-narrated · Restrooms available · ~3 hours · No strenuous activity required
$45–$65/pp Senior pricing available
Whale Watching Catamaran (Point Adolphus)
Heated enclosed main cabin with large windows · Can stay seated and warm · Naturalist narration · Humpback whales nearly guaranteed · ~2.5 hours · Moderate boat motion — advise sea sickness patch if Mom is sensitive
$120–$160/pp · Book through Princess early
Juneau Gold Panning & Historic Tour
Guided narrated tour of Juneau's gold rush history · Pan for real Alaskan gold · Seated demonstrations · Comfortable for all ages and fitness levels · No strenuous activity · Great keepsake experience
$45–$75/pp
PORT: SKAGWAY — 🚂 THE TRAIN DAY
White Pass & Yukon Route Railway
BOOK THIS FIRST. Historic narrow-gauge railway built during the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush. 3-hour roundtrip to the Canadian border. Vintage climate-controlled rail cars with panoramic windows. Stunning views of Dead Horse Gulch, steel cantilever bridges, and mountain glaciers. Comfortable seats — no standing required. Perfect for all mobility levels. This is Alaska's most iconic rail experience and sells out months in advance.
$140–$175/pp Senior pricing available
Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
Free · Flat paved walking on Broadway Street · National Park ranger tours depart from the visitor center · Gold rush-era buildings preserved exactly as they were in 1898 · Short walks, interesting history, no fitness requirement · Pair with the railway for a full day
Free · Ranger-led tours at no charge
PORT: VICTORIA, B.C. (EVENING)
Afternoon Tea at The Fairmont Empress Hotel
Victoria's most iconic experience · Formal tea service in the legendary Fairmont Empress ballroom · White glove service · 3-tiered afternoon tea with finger sandwiches, scones, and pastries · Perfect for Mom · Reserve ahead — very popular in summer season
~$75–$95 CAD/pp (~$55–$70 USD) · Must reserve in advance
Inner Harbour Evening Walk
Flat paved waterfront promenade · Buskers, horse-drawn carriages, and the illuminated Parliament Buildings · Easy stroll at your own pace · No booking needed · Start point is directly at the cruise dock · Excellent photo opportunities at dusk
Free
Butchart Gardens Evening Visit
World-famous 55-acre gardens, illuminated at night · Paved paths throughout (some slopes, but accessible routes available) · Saturday evenings include fireworks · ~20-min shuttle from the ship · Allow 2–3 hours · Gorgeous for photos and leisurely strolling
~$45–$55 CAD/pp (~$33–$41 USD) · Shuttle additional
Agent's Note: Book the White Pass Railway and Whale Watching the moment your cruise is confirmed — both regularly sell out 3–4 months in advance. The Fairmont Empress tea should also be reserved as early as possible. Everything else can be booked onboard or at the pier. For all excursions, I can arrange pre-booking through Princess or independent operators — just let me know your preferences and I'll handle it.
